passage:
A school installed a small earthquake sensor connected to an alarm system. It could give a warning only seconds before strong shaking arrived.
Some students said a few seconds were useless. The science teacher disagreed. A few seconds could let people move away from windows, stop machines, or protect their heads.
The class practiced what to do when the alarm sounded. At first, they moved slowly. After practice, their response became quicker.
The sensor did not prevent earthquakes. It gave time.
Students learned that safety is often measured in small amounts. A few seconds may not sound like much, but in danger, they can matter.
